From my understanding, KServe currently does not support running models on multi-instance GPUs, but the upstream vLLM seems to support it. Something like this won't work:

```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: multilingual-e5-large-instruct
spec:
  predictor:
    model:
      modelFormat:
        name: huggingface

        - --model_name=multilingual-e5-large-instruct
        - --model_id=intfloat/multilingual-e5-large-instruct
      resources:
        limits:
          nvidia.com/mig-1g.12gb: "2"
      env:
        - name: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
          value: "0"
```

There are no explicit error messages, but the InferenceService fails to create any workloads (Pods/Deployments/ReplicaSets). Maybe a validating webhook does not allow this (see [allowed constants](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/ae964630d9c480af199e2bfa77fb99d47915048f/pkg/constants/constants.go#L246), for example), maybe this is a much more complicated problem, I am ufortunately not familiar with KServe architecture.

That being said, this vLLM-based solution will work:
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: vllm-e5-mig
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: vllm-e5
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: vllm-e5
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: vllm
        image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.9.0.1
        command:
        - "python3"
        - "-m"
        - "vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server"
        - "--model"

        - "--port=8000"

        resources:

        env:
        - name: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
          value: "0"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: vllm-e5-service
spec:
  selector:
    app: vllm-e5
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 8000
  type: ClusterIP 
```

body:
/kind bug

**What steps did you take and what happened:**
I would like to deploy my ML model with KServe's Inference Service. 
I trained ML model with scikit-learn SVM classifier and sklearn's iris dataset. Then, I convert .pkl model to .onnx format with code:
```
import onnxmltools
import onnxruntime
import pickle
from skl2onnx.common.data_types import FloatTensorType, Int64TensorType

with open("model.pkl", "rb") as f:
    model = pickle.load(f)

onnx_model = onnxmltools.convert_sklearn(model=model,initial_types=[('float_input', FloatTensorType([1, 4]))])

print(onnx_model)

onnxmltools.utils.save_model(onnx_model, "model.onnx")

sess = onnxruntime.InferenceSession("model.onnx")

print("In", [(i.name, i.type, i.shape) for i in sess.get_inputs()])
  
print("Out", [(i.name, i.type, i.shape) for i in sess.get_outputs()])

input_data = [[5,1,1,1]]

result = sess.run(['probabilities'], {'float_input':input_data})

print(result)
```

body:
When an InferenceService can load multiple models when can we mark an InferenceService ready?
**Approach 1: An InferenceService is ready when all the models are ready**
pros: 
1) k8s can help reject requests coming into this pod as the pod won't be ready

cons:
1) If there are 1000 models in a pod, if one model is not ready then all other models can not receive traffic
2) If a large model need to be loaded, then it will blocks traffic for all other models

**Approach 2: An InferenceService is ready as long as an empty model server is up**
pros: 
1) one model that is not ready won't block the traffic to other models

cons:
1) when an InferenceService need to be scaled up, users may expect that a new replica is only ready when all models are ready
title: Manage virtual service route for each model in for multi-model InferenceService

This is because knative and kubeflow both create an istio [Gateway resource](https://istio.io/docs/reference/config/networking/v1alpha3/gateway/) and the kubeflow entry doesn't include port 80 whereas knative does. So port 80 traffic is unsecured (and still open because not covered by the kubeflow auth envoyfilter) and is routed by istio to the knative services as it matches the knative gateway record.

I can move the knative gateway to the default https port but then there's a conflict with the kubeflow gateway and requests do not get routed to the services. The only configuration I've able to get working with auth is putting the knative gateway on a different port entirely (e.g. 15443). I suspect it would also work if I were to create [a distinct entrypoint IP for knative](https://knative.dev/docs/serving/setting-up-custom-ingress-gateway/), though that would require additional changes to the auth setup (to allow that redirectUri).

@yanniszark [has suggested](https://github.com/kubeflow/kfserving/issues/196#issuecomment-506827346) this could be addressed by getting knative to use the kubeflow gateway. But I've tried to do that without success. Knative lets you [repoint to a different external gateway service](https://knative.dev/docs/serving/setting-up-custom-ingress-gateway/) but I've not been able to point to a different isitio Gateway (changing the config-istio configmap didn't work for me).

I've also considered changing kubeflow to use the knative-gateway but that would be a big change.
title: shared auth with kubeflow
